claim: Individuals who were neither parties nor privies to consent decrees are not precluded from bringing independent Title VII discrimination claims based on actions taken pursuant to those decrees, and a consent decree entered pursuant to voluntary settlement provides no greater protection against charges of illegal discrimination than a voluntary affirmative action plan.
initial_reasoning: The decision reported at 833 F.2d 1492 holds that a consent decree entered in a voluntary settlement does not immunize third‑party individuals from filing separate Title VII discrimination actions arising from conduct undertaken under the decree, and it affirms that such a decree offers no greater shield than an ordinary affirmative‑action plan. This directly supports the claim, though the precise facts of the case are not widely cited, giving moderate certainty.
